'''Sagar Sengupta''' is an Indian cancer biologist, a scientist at the [[National Institute of Immunology, India]] and Director, National Institute of Biomedical Genomics, Kalyani, India. Known for his studies on genome integrity, [[tumor suppressor gene]] and [[oncogenes]], Sengupta is an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies namely the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]. He has been a Jagadish Chandra Bose (JC Bose) Fellow since 2018. The [[Department of Biotechnology]] of the Government of India awarded him the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to biosciences, in 2011.

== Biography ==
[[File:Kolkata univ jeroje.jpg|thumb|University of Calcutta]]
Sagar Sengupta was born in the Indian state of [[West Bengal]], earned a postgraduate degree from the [[University of Calcutta]] and secured a PhD from the [[Indian Institute of Science]].<ref name="Sagar Sengupta on NII">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nii.res.in/research/sagar-sengupta |title=Sagar Sengupta on NII |date=2018-01-27 |website=www.nii.res.in |access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref> He did his post doctoral studies at the Institut de Genetique et de Biologie Moleculaire et Cellulaire (IGBMC) in [[Strasbourg]], France and completed it at the [[National Cancer Institute]] of the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref name="Sagar Sengupta, profile in India Cancer Research Database">{{Cite web |url=http://www.incredb.org/investigator.php?incredb_id=415 |title=Sagar Sengupta, profile in India Cancer Research Database |date=2018-01-27 |website=www.incredb.org |access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref> Subsequently, he joined the [[National Institute of Immunology, India]] in 2004 as a faculty. He served in National Institute of Immunology till 2022 as a Grade VII Staff Scientist.<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P17-1761 |title=Indian fellow |date=2018-01-25 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2018-01-25}}</ref> In November 2022, Sengupta became the Director of National Institute of Biomedical Genomics, Kalyani, West Bengal on deputation from National Institute of Immunology. From November 2023, he hasalso been Director (Additional Charge) of National Brain Research Centre, Manesar, Haryana. The permanent residence of Sengupta is in [[Gurgaon]], [[Haryana]].<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |title=NASI fellows |date=2018-01-25 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=2018-01-25 |archive-date=16 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316043224/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Professional profile ==
Sengupta's research focus is on the changes in the signaling pathways during cancer development and he has carried out studies on the tumour suppressor genes and oncogenes.<ref name="Sagar Sengupta on NII" /> During his post-doctoral days at the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH), he undertook a project on NIH grant to study the ''Determination of regulatory mechanisms for BLM helicase''.<ref name="Determination of regulatory mechanisms for BLM helicase">{{Cite journal |url=http://grantome.com/grant/NIH/R01-TW007302-04 |title=Determination of regulatory mechanisms for BLM helicase |last=Sagar |first=Sengupta |date=2018-01-27 |website=Grantome |language=en |access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles<ref name="On Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Bc4SKwgAAAAJ&hl=en |title=On Google Scholar |date=2018-01-20 |publisher=Google Scholar |access-date=2018-01-20}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and [[ResearchGate]], an online repository of scientific articles has listed over 50 of them.<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sagar_Sengupta |title=On ResearchGate |date=2018-01-20 |access-date=2018-01-20}}</ref> The complete list of his publications can be found at: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/myncbi/1t7wpVLc8yt/bibliography/public/

He has also undertaken several projects on behalf of the government agencies such as the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]], the Science and Engineering Research Board, the [[Department of Biotechnology]] and the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] and the Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences as the principal investigator<ref name="Sagar Sengupta, profile in India Cancer Research Database" /> and is associated with the Department of Biotechnology as a member of its Task force on Cancer Biology, the expert committee on Promotion and Popularization of Biotechnology and the Expert Committee for Twinning RD program for North Eastern Region.<ref name="Sagar Sengupta - Speakers - Indian Academy of Sciences">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/MYM2017/Speakers/Sagar_Sengupta |title=Sagar Sengupta - Speakers - Indian Academy of Sciences |date=2018-01-27 |website=www.ias.ac.in |language=en |access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Sengupta received the Best Thesis Award for his doctoral thesis from the Indian Institute of Science in 1997.<ref name="Sagar Sengupta on NII" /> The [[Department of Biotechnology]] (DBT) of the Government of India awarded him the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 2011.<ref name="Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development">{{Cite web |url=http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |title=Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development |date=2016 |publisher=Department of Biotechnology |access-date=2017-11-20 |archive-date=4 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304191331/http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> The [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] elected him as a fellow in 2012<ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI Year Book 2015 |date=2018-01-25 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=2018-01-25 |archive-date=6 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806211716/http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and he became an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 2017.<ref name="Fellowship - Indian Academy of Sciences">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/listing/fellows/S |title=Fellowship - Indian Academy of Sciences |date=2018-01-27 |website=www.ias.ac.in |language=en |access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref> He is also a member of the [[Guha Research Conference]].<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He has been a Jagadish Chandra Bose (JC Bose) Fellow since 2018.
